canonical.title: Generating the itenium-ui API client from Forge's OpenAPI document

parent.title: The React state stack for Itenium.Forge in 2026: the Redux question dissolves

siblings.title: Is Redux still the right answer for a new React 19 app in 2026?
siblings.summary: Redux is healthy but no longer the default: for a greenfield React 19 SPA talking to a REST API, TanStack Query plus a small Zustand store wins.

siblings.title: Server-state layer for a React 19 + Vite SPA on a .NET API: TanStack Query wins
siblings.summary: TanStack Query is the correct server-state layer for itenium-ui; Register.defaultError makes ProblemDetails a first-class typed error.

siblings.title: Client state after the query cache: Zustand vs Jotai vs RTK vs plain React 19
siblings.summary: Once TanStack Query owns server state, the residual client state is roughly one persisted preferences store — take Zustand.

siblings.title: The router is a state manager: TanStack Router for itenium-ui
siblings.summary: TanStack Router makes filters/sort/pagination typed URL state instead of Redux slices.

siblings.title: Auth & session state for a React 19 SPA on Forge: kill the localStorage plan
siblings.summary: Use react-oidc-context with an in-memory access token; serve capabilities from /me instead of the token.

sources.title: https://saschb2b.com/blog/typesafe-api-codegen-2026
sources.claim: 2026 consensus in React API codegen is to generate framework-agnostic queryOptions/mutationOptions rather than bespoke hooks; Hey API recommended for REST, Orval noted for built-in MSW mocks.

sources.title: https://github.com/openapi-ts/openapi-typescript/discussions/2559
sources.claim: openapi-fetch, openapi-react-query and openapi-metadata were moved to maintenance mode in the project's 2026 roadmap; only openapi-typescript (types) keeps getting invested in.

sources.title: https://kubb.dev/docs/5.x/guide/comparison
sources.claim: Kubb's own comparison: all four (Kubb, Orval, Hey API, openapi-typescript) support TS types, React Query, Zod and MSW handlers; Kubb is plugin/AST-based and uniquely emits Vue Query, Cypress and Redoc output; openapi-typescript's satellite packages are in maintenance mode.

sources.title: https://orval.dev/docs/guides/react-query/
sources.claim: Orval's react-query client emits, per operation, a request function, a query-key factory (e.g. getShowPetByIdQueryKey) and a useXxx hook; useInfinite/useInfiniteQueryParam and per-operation overrides are supported.

sources.title: https://orval.dev/docs/reference/configuration/output/
sources.claim: Orval output options: mode tags-split, client react-query, httpClient fetch|axios, schemas, mock.generators (msw + faker), clean, formatter, baseUrl.runtime, override.mutator, override.useDates, override.query, override.operations.

sources.title: https://orval.dev/docs/versions/v8/
sources.claim: Orval v8 (Jan 2026) is ESM-only (Node 22.18+), defaults httpClient to fetch, auto-detects Zod 3 vs 4, replaces override.useNativeEnums with enumGenerationType, and improves OpenAPI 3.1 compliance.

sources.title: https://heyapi.dev/openapi-ts/plugins/tanstack-query
sources.claim: Hey API's TanStack Query plugin generates queryOptions, infiniteQueryOptions, mutationOptions and query keys rather than hooks, and works across React/Vue/Svelte/Solid/Angular.

sources.title: https://github.com/hey-api/hey-api/issues/3270
sources.claim: Hey API only added true discriminated-union generation (TS unions + z.discriminatedUnion) in 2026 via issue #3270 / PR #3780; before that it emitted intersections and plain string discriminator fields.

sources.title: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/57982
sources.claim: Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi emits polymorphic types as anyOf with renamed derived schemas and omits the OpenAPI discriminator object that Swashbuckle emits; issue is open and in the Backlog milestone.

sources.title: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/openapi/aspnetcore-openapi?view=aspnetcore-10.0
sources.claim: .NET 10's Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi defaults to OpenAPI 3.1, exposes document/schema transformer APIs, and supports build-time document emission via the Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Server package (GetDocument target).

sources.title: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/openapi/include-metadata?view=aspnetcore-10.0
sources.claim: .NET enums without a JsonConverter are emitted as type: integer in the OpenAPI schema; only with JsonStringEnumConverter does the schema carry the string enum values. ProblemDetails responses must be declared via ProducesResponseType/TypedResults metadata.

sources.title: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/61303
sources.claim: Known .NET bug: the built-in OpenAPI generator can omit the enum type/values even when JsonStringEnumConverter is applied, requiring a schema transformer workaround.

sources.title: https://codingdroplets.com/kiota-vs-nswag-vs-refitter-dotnet-typed-api-client-2026
sources.claim: In 2026 NSwag's OpenAPI 3.1 support is partial and can produce incorrect models for complex schemas; Kiota has better 3.1 compliance but targets multi-language SDK scenarios.

sources.title: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openapi/kiota/quickstarts/typescript
sources.claim: Kiota's TypeScript language support is officially in preview, with features not fully supported and source-breaking changes expected.

sources.title: https://github.com/microsoft/kiota/discussions/3966
sources.claim: Kiota maintainers/community discussion enumerating openapi-generator's shortcomings (Java toolchain, template sprawl, inconsistent generator quality).

sources.title: https://redux-toolkit.js.org/rtk-query/usage/code-generation
sources.claim: RTK Query ships @rtk-query/codegen-openapi, which generates typed endpoints and, with hooks: true, useQuery/useMutation exports from an OpenAPI schema.

sources.title: https://tanstack.com/query/v5/docs/framework/react/guides/does-this-replace-client-state
sources.claim: TanStack Query's own position: once async/server data moves into Query, the genuinely global client state that remains is usually very small.

sources.title: https://orval.dev/docs/guides/custom-axios/
sources.claim: Orval lets a custom mutator export an ErrorType alias that overrides the error type of every generated react-query/swr hook — the hook to wire RFC 7807 ProblemDetails as the single error type.

sources.title: https://github.com/orval-labs/orval/issues/3149
sources.claim: Orval v8 bug: an OpenAPI 3.0 schema with only nullable: true and no type emits invalid TypeScript (an interface with a union body); fixed by emitting a type alias.

sources.title: https://github.com/orval-labs/orval/issues/2933
sources.claim: Orval Zod generation in split mode has multiple reported codegen bugs requiring post-processing workarounds.

sources.title: https://nx.dev/recipes/running-tasks/configure-outputs
sources.claim: Nx caches a target's declared outputs, so an openapi codegen target declared with inputs (the spec) and outputs (the generated folder) is restored from cache instead of re-run.

sources.title: https://codewithmukesh.com/blog/dotnet-swagger-alternatives-openapi/
sources.claim: Swashbuckle was removed from the .NET default template but is not deprecated; Swashbuckle 10.x supports .NET 10 with opt-in OpenAPI 3.1, while Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi is the native default for new projects.

sources.title: https://orval.dev/docs/reference/configuration/input/
sources.claim: Orval's input supports a file path or URL target, tag/schema filters, and an override.transformer hook that mutates the OpenAPI document before validation — the escape hatch for .NET spec quirks.

sources.title: https://openapi-ts.dev/openapi-react-query/
sources.claim: openapi-react-query is the thin TanStack Query wrapper over openapi-fetch — a runtime wrapper, not a codegen step, so it produces no per-operation hooks or query keys.

sources.title: https://github.com/orval-labs/orval/issues/3246
sources.claim: Open Orval bug (Apr 2026): enumGenerationType: 'enum' with $ref'd enum properties emits an empty import in generated mock files.

sources.title: https://dev.to/nyaomaru/which-openapi-codegen-should-you-choose-openapi-typescript-vs-hey-api-vs-orval-vs-kubb-100p
sources.claim: Practitioner comparison: openapi-typescript for types only, Orval when you want everything generated, Kubb for maximum control; Hey API positioned as the successor to openapi-typescript-codegen.

sources.title: https://github.com/OpenAPI-Qraft/openapi-qraft
sources.claim: openapi-qraft generates proxy-based typed TanStack Query interfaces from an OpenAPI schema but is a very small project (~96 stars).

sources.title: https://github.com/domaindrivendev/Swashbuckle.AspNetCore/issues/2944
sources.claim: Swashbuckle bug report: ProblemDetails is not always generated as a Swagger schema, which leaves the error type untyped in generated clients unless responses are explicitly annotated.

sources.title: https://orval.dev/docs/guides/client-with-zod/
sources.claim: Orval generates Zod schemas as a second output entry with client: 'zod' and fileExtension: '.zod.ts' to avoid filename collisions with the client output.

sources.title: https://www.pkgpulse.com/guides/orval-vs-openapi-typescript-vs-kubb-openapi-client-2026
sources.claim: 2026 guide: start with openapi-typescript + openapi-fetch for simplicity, move to Orval when React Query integration matters, Kubb when you need custom generation patterns.
